items.text: The Haitian djouba study now plays its own drums. Opening it loads a "Haitian djouba drums" sound set: the kata (stick on wood), the boula (small goatskin drum), the manman (large goatskin drum) and the tchatcha shaker, one per track. Before, its tracks played the generic drum kit, so the goatskin drums did not sound like goatskin. The four drums are also in the colour menus as "Djouba: ...". They are synthesized sketches from descriptions, not heard by a drummer. The Lebanese study still plays the generic kit; its own drums come with the Lebanese kit.

The sliders in the Index now look and behave like the ones in the heads-up display: a thin track, the readout turns to the accent colour once you change a slider, and double-tapping the slider's name glides it back to its default. On Size, the name's double-tap is the same as the Default grid button.
New "Default grid (12 × 12)" button under Size. Importing a MIDI piece makes the grid 16 × 16 and leaves it that way; one tap puts it back to the standard 12 × 12 and clears the imported piece.

New sound kit: Haitian rara. Pick "Haitian rara" in the sound sets to load eight synthesized voices, one per colour: three bamboo vaksin trumpets and a fourth a little over a semitone above the third, a tin kone horn, a goatskin tanbou with its slap, a kata stick with a kes rattle, and a graj scraper with tcha-tcha and a faint whistle.

The vaksin are tuned by offsets from a centre of 220 Hz (0, +310, +590 and +690 cents), not a standard scale, and each always sounds at its own pitch whatever row it lands on. They are sketches from published descriptions of rara, not a transcription, and I have not had them heard by a rara player.
Each voice is also on its own in the colour menus, as "Rara: ...".

Colours and marks are now checkboxes. Tap to add or remove one (one always stays on); tap twice quickly to choose just that one. Drawing with several on deals from them, as a shuffled bag by default: every chosen colour or mark comes up before any repeats, so a stroke is evenly mixed. A small shuffle button appears when you have more than one on; press it to pick at random instead.
Saved looks carry the chosen colours, marks and deal order.
Hold's rings are bolder and travel farther, and they appear only while a held sound is actually sounding. With Hold on and nothing held, the hand stays still.
The waveforms in the tempo bar fade out toward the speaker and the BPM, and are gone by the bar's rounded ends.
While Hold is on, its hand sends rings out from both sides, like the rings from the fingertip on the touch button.

The stopwatch starts and pauses the performance clock with a tap; hold it for the Performance settings. It turns yellow only while the performance is armed or running, not just because a custom shape exists or the clock has moved.
The MIDI button asks the browser for controllers again on every tap, which revives one that was dropped. Hold it to map knobs. Both buttons carry the corner marker for their hold.
